summary: Delegated-token swap mid-stream + proxy base64-trim causes duplicate webhook executions (Go orchestration)
description: Customer reported duplicate outbound webhook deliveries from their orchestrator after a long-running streaming session where the Go SDK refreshed delegated credentials mid-stream. The duplicates happen only when the orchestrator refreshes a short-lived delegated token during an in-flight stream and the edge proxy performs header canonicalization that trims base64 padding. This results in the same logical idempotency salt being presented in two different canonical forms, and our service treats them as different idempotency scopes, which leads to duplicate downstream webhook invocations. Customer is seeing financial and operational impact (duplicate downstream jobs).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming session using Redwood Go SDK v0.9.8 from an orchestration service that performs long-running function calls (external webhooks).

2) Configure the orchestrator to use delegated short-lived credentials and forcibly rotate the delegated token ~30s after stream start (we reproduced with a token refresh triggered by background credential refresh code path).
3) Ensure an edge-side proxy is present (customer uses an edge accelerant that trims headers for canonicalization).

4) Trigger a function/tool call that attaches an idempotency salt (SDK-provided header: X-Redwood-Idempotency) and allow the SDK to perform a retry when the stream experiences a transient 503 during rotation.
5) Observe outbound webhook being delivered twice to the customer endpoint despite a single logical function invocation in the client.
observed_behavior: Two POSTs to the customer's webhook endpoint for a single logical tool call. In our request logs we see two different canonical forms of the idempotency header for the same session: one with base64 padding ("xyz+abc==") and one with padding trimmed ("xyz+abc"). Server treats these as distinct idempotency keys and executes the tool twice.
expected_behavior: A single tool/webhook invocation per logical idempotency scope — SDK and server should canonicalize the idempotency salt consistently across token refreshes and proxies so that retries are deduplicated as expected.
logs: 2026-03-12T15:03:31.229Z DEBUG outgoing-call request_id=req-7f3a X-Redwood-Idempotency=xyz+abc== Authorization=Bearer eyJ...old
2026-03-12T15:03:31.789Z INFO retry-schedule backoff_ms=250 request_id=req-7f3b X-Redwood-Idempotency=xyz+abc Authorization=Bearer eyJ...new
investigation_notes: Edge proxy is trimming '=' characters when normalizing headers; this is an optimization in their canonicalization codepath and not reversible on our side once header arrives transformed.

Go SDK constructs the idempotency salt as base64(salt) and includes padding by default. When the delegated token rotates mid-stream, the SDK reattaches the same salt value but the proxy normalization yields a different header form for the retried request.

Server idempotency check is currently exact-string match on X-Redwood-Idempotency + session namespace. No canonicalization step is applied server-side, so differing canonical forms are treated as distinct keys.

We reproduced internally by running the customer's edge proxy image and forcing a token refresh during a streaming function call. Duplicate webhook posts matched the customer's timeline and request IDs.
Related historical tickets looked at: SUP-716121 (hsm salt rotation) — similar theme but different root cause; SUP-992233 (midflight jwt rotate) — referenced for rotation timing patterns.
workarounds: Customer-side temporary: enable idempotent dedupe on their webhook receiver (accept and ignore duplicate POSTs by checking payload or idempotency header equivalence allowing for base64 padding variations).
Proxy-side temporary: disable header padding trim (edge config change) so headers are forwarded verbatim to Redwood. We've provided the config flag the edge vendor can toggle.

SDK temporary: have the orchestrator normalize idempotency salt before sending (strip or add '=' padding consistently). We provided a small snippet for Go to normalize to padding-stripped form: base64.StdEncoding.WithPadding(base64.NoPadding).EncodeToString(...)

Short-term server-side mitigation: added a best-effort canonicalization step in the request ingestion path to trim trailing '=' from X-Redwood-Idempotency for incoming requests from edge-proxy subnets (rolled to prod on 2026-03-13 03:20 UTC). This reduces but does not fully eliminate risk for other canonicalization variants.
resolution: Partial mitigation deployed: server now applies a normalized compare (trim trailing '=' in idempotency header) for requests originating from known edge-proxy IP blocks, which reduced duplicates for the customer by ~95%. Customer accepted webhook-level dedupe as immediate fail-safe. Engineering will implement a robust canonicalization and normalization contract in the SDK/server so idempotency checks are invariant to harmless header transformations. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Target fix: SDK v0.10.2 and server-side contract changes; tracking PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/9876. Follow-up: add a confluence doc describing 'Idempotency normalization contract' and update SDKs with explicit per-action idempotency_key parameter.

DEVREL: Publish guidance and a code snippet for Go/TS/Python showing stable idempotency key handling (owner: Priya Shah) — target 2026-03-20
